comments.body:
=== SESSION: e369 Jira DC — the exit bar that closed the criterion-vs-working gap; 9 certified closes; gates proven fallible ===

--- OUTCOME ---
Epic e369: **56 of 58 descendants closed, exit bar MET and ticked.** The DC harness went GREEN end to
end for the first time — run **30964805133** at `c3fb869ab5`: `62 passed, 1 xfailed`, canary
`collected=63 executed=62 skipped=1`. Nine tickets closed and certified this session (2e47, 3b5f,
465d, 259b, 2c93, 18a4, 9f26, 4b9e, 34c2), every one with a real `completion-verifier: PASS`, none
forced. Open: 9790 (Gerrit 1406, LLM-Review +1) and 8390.

--- THE RULING THAT MATTERED MOST ---
**"The epic's goal is to deliver Jira DC functionality without bugs. Resolve the failures represented
by this result, not remove the failing tests."** I was drifting toward filing a test-hygiene ticket to
`xfail` three permanently-red cells. That would have hidden three real DC defects behind green CI.

The operator then approved an **exit bar** as a 14th epic criterion: *the live DC harness job is GREEN
end to end (0 failed cells)*. This closed the structural gap that let **13/13 criteria be met while
three live cells failed** — none of the 13 required the harness to pass, so criterion-completeness was
never evidence the feature worked. Cost, accepted knowingly: the edit staled the epic's own
plan-review attestation (`stale-material`).

--- THE THREE CELLS: NEVER PASSED, NOT REGRESSED ---
Operator asked the right discriminating question ("or there has been regression"). Measured per-cell
failing sets across ALL 12 harness runs from 30834117797 to 30951453979:
`inbound_set_subtask_parent`, `outbound_set_subtask_parent`, `outbound_clear_parent` failed **12/12**.
Never a regression — never implemented. The same data proved the harness DETECTS fixes (6 -> 3
failures over the window, six other cells dropping out at identifiable runs), which is what made the
conclusion trustworthy rather than an assumption about a broken suite.

--- MY OWN TICKET WAS WRONG, TWICE, AND THE GATE CAUGHT IT ---
I authored 9f26 and briefed an agent from it. Two premises were FALSE:
1. `set_parent` is at `_hierarchy.py:100`, NOT `transport.py` — I inherited 39c1's citation without
   re-checking, and 465d's split had moved it. (So the file collision I sequenced 9790 behind never
   existed.)
2. **"The two gates are disjoint, so no reconcile pass can carry a parent-set on DC at all" is
   REFUTED.** Since 39c1 the non-sub-task branch writes the Epic Link, and
   `test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS` was ALREADY green. I read 39c1's
   PROBLEM STATEMENT as current state without checking whether 39c1's own fix had moved past it.

The real defect was **silence**: `_resolve_local_parent` returned `(False, None)` for a non-epic
parent — byte-identical to its "unbound, retry" return — so `parent` never entered `fields` and 39c1's
whole `record_parent_divergence`/`bridge_alerts` apparatus was structurally UNREACHABLE.
**And the three cells were WRONG ORACLES, not symptoms** — each asserted an operation the platform
cannot perform. That distinction is why re-homing was the remedy and why it was NOT "accepting failing
tests".

--- BOTH GATES GREEN ON A DEFECTIVE CHANGE ---
**Gerrit 1398 reached `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`, fully submittable, containing a real bug**:
the divergence recording sat where it could not see `canonical_remote`, so it fired even when the
tracker already held the correct parent — alerting every pass for every such ticket, inverting the
alert's meaning. Caught by adversarial self-review, not by either gate. **Its mutation checks missed
it because the fixture hardcoded `remote_parent_id: None` — a mutation check only tests the axes its
fixture varies.** Abandoned rather than amended. This is the second independent instance (with 3787)
of "both votes green" != correct.

That lesson then paid off: on 9790 a mutation SURVIVED (an unusable read treated as ready), and the
missing cell was added rather than declaring six-of-six.

--- FOUR SUBSTANTIVE PLAN-REVIEW BLOCKS, ALL ACCURATE ---
* 3b5f — the plan named ONE test consumer to delete; eight more referenced the removed symbols.
* 18a4 — a transport-only fix would not have resolved the report (all three DC readers feed
  `fetch_snapshot`'s three fail-opens; `fetcher.py` named neither stall error).
* 18a4 again — my plan claimed the abort was "instrumented" by `_call_logged`'s WARNING. FALSE:
  `_call_logged` logs only inside `except Exception`, and on a stall `search_issues` SUCCEEDS, so the
  guard raises outside its `try`. `_paged_search` has ZERO `logger.` calls. Corrected the text rather
  than adding a redundant log (the raise already names key, offset and JQL).
* 9f26 — independently found the same two false premises I had written.

--- MEASUREMENT BEAT DOCUMENTATION, AGAIN (3rd and 4th capability-map retractions) ---
* **req-0022 REFUTED**: the map claims ids 10003 and 10004 are both named `Task`. Run 30951453979
  measured `[('10002','Task'), ('10003','Sub-task'), ('10000','Epic')]` — ONE `Task`, and 10003 is
  `Sub-task`. Critically this is a **SAME-DIGEST contradiction**: the `FROM` pin at `d394a70529` is
  byte-identical to the recorded digest, so it is not image drift. That is the one class a digest
  gate provably cannot catch — the core argument for a9bd.
* **2c93 dissolved by live Cloud probe** (operator-authorized): Cloud accepts a 255-char label
  (HTTP 201, byte-exact round-trip) and rejects 256 (HTTP 400) — IDENTICAL to DC. The reported
  divergence does not exist; the per-deployment ceiling would have been machinery for a difference
  that was never there. Probe cleaned up in both systems (DELETE 204, GET 404, `rebar search` 0 hits).

--- THE PARENT-CLEAR INCIDENT: BOTH HYPOTHESES TRUE, OF DISJOINT POPULATIONS ---
Operator hypothesis (reconciler clearing parents) and mine (never parented) were BOTH right:
* The 7 tickets my orphan sweep found were **never parented** — CREATE with `parent_id: ""`, no
  clearing event ever.
* The reconciler **did** clear 63 parents once, run 30828160906, 11 seconds, commit `b8062b10e9`
  (verified: 64 files / 64 insertions). Rule is exact: cleared iff BOUND and parent is NOT an epic
  (605+ epic-parented, zero cleared). Already fixed on main 40 minutes later.
* `''` vs `None` is ONE write path, two representations — `""` is the reconciler's fingerprint.
* **e369 is clean**: only 2 of 63 victims were in its tree, both already restored. 57 remain orphaned
  repo-wide, stuck because their parents are closed (`ed5e`).
* **My "natural experiment is running" claim was WRONG** — zero reconciles had run since 19:00 UTC, so
  nothing could have reverted. I would have read a null result as confirmation.

--- FOUR FALSE CONCLUSIONS FROM UNCHECKED EMPTY SCANS (the recurring self-inflicted wound) ---
1. Regex had `jira-dc` but not `jira DC` (space) — missed obvious orphans.
2. `rebar list` carries **no `description` field**, so a body scan matched nothing and returned a
   confident "1 candidate".
3. Grepped the WORKING TREE (`3b830a514c`) while the merged code was on `gerrit/main` — every 18a4
   symbol read as absent.
4. `grep -oE "[0-9]+ (skipped|...)"` spliced across `executed=62 skipped=1` and reported "62 skipped".
**An empty or suspiciously clean result is not evidence until the scan itself is checked against a
case known to exist.**

--- OPERATIONAL FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING ---
* **CI selects by MARKER**: `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`. A `tests/unit` path subset
  MISSES unmarked tests under `tests/integration/` — that gap cost a CI cycle (the
  `EXPECTED_LEAF_PAIRS` drift guard). Correct selection: 10165+ tests vs 8077.
* **`git commit --amend -F -` DROPS the `Change-Id` trailer** — mints a new change instead of a
  patchset, which is how a green-but-wrong change was left sitting submittable.
* **3787 discipline paid off 3 times**: when `gerrit/main` moves past a change's base, submitting lets
  Gerrit rebase server-side into a tree CI never validated. Rebased locally + re-gated instead.
* **Store lock contention is real** (ab54/7084): a `rebar edit` failed with `flock: could not acquire
  lock after 60s` and did NOT land. Retry and confirm every write by READING THE OUTPUT.
* **Attestations go `stale-code` once their own change lands**, and `--status` is HEAD-relative — run
  it from the same worktree you will close from.
* **df3a is intermittent, not deterministic**: 259b's close failed twice with an identical empty-object
  payload and succeeded on the third. I was one data point from escalating it wrongly.

--- STATE HANDED OVER ---
* `9790` — Gerrit **1406** (`LLM-Review +1`, Verified pending). All 5 ACs verified against the change.
  Shared stdlib-only `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py`; both consumers DELEGATE, so AC4's drift
  cannot recur. Sibling `4a6d` filed: a THIRD live-DC channel (the capability-map workflow) has the
  same weak gate and is worse — it REPORTS rather than fails.
* `8390` — in flight (CREATE emit + ACLI attach fallback parity).
* **Epic close needs a fresh `review-plan e369`** — `stale-material` from the exit-bar edit. Held until
  the last children land, since each landing change stales it again.
* **UNRESOLVED**: `a9bd`/`6194`/`6a74` have been re-parented into e369 **twice** after removal,
  including a9bd which the operator explicitly ordered unparented. Every write is authored
  `RebarBotNava` (the shared bot identity) with no session recorded, so attribution is impossible from
  the event log. Removed a third time without re-adding `relates_to` (the only correlated variable —
  but 9a46 got identical treatment and stayed out, so that hypothesis is weak). If it recurs, it wants
  a `/rebar-debug`.
* **`8a5e` (open)**: four MORE single-file AST guards vacuous by the same rot as 34c2/59b2. Third
  occurrence of the class; that is where the remaining exposure is.
* Pre-existing on main, not ours: `test_plan_review_resign.py::test_public_resign_preserves_mixed_
  child_scope_and_validity` errors under parallel execution ("leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT"),
  passes in isolation.

3. Grepped the WORKING TREE (`3b830a514c`) while the merged code was on `gerrit/main` — every 18a4
   symbol read as absent.
4. `grep -oE "[0-9]+ (skipped|...)"` spliced across `executed=62 skipped=1` and reported "62 skipped".
**An empty or suspiciously clean result is not evidence until the scan itself is checked against a
case known to exist.**

--- OPERATIONAL FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING ---
* **CI selects by MARKER**: `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`. A `tests/unit` path subset
  MISSES unmarked tests under `tests/integration/` — that gap cost a CI cycle (the
  `EXPECTED_LEAF_PAIRS` drift guard). Correct selection: 10165+ tests vs 8077.
* **`git commit --amend -F -` DROPS the `Change-Id` trailer** — mints a new change instead of a
  patchset, which is how a green-but-wrong change was left sitting submittable.
* **3787 discipline paid off 3 times**: when `gerrit/main` moves past a change's base, submitting lets
  Gerrit rebase server-side into a tree CI never validated. Rebased locally + re-gated instead.
* **Store lock contention is real** (ab54/7084): a `rebar edit` failed with `flock: could not acquire
  lock after 60s` and did NOT land. Retry and confirm every write by READING THE OUTPUT.
* **Attestations go `stale-code` once their own change lands**, and `--status` is HEAD-relative — run
  it from the same worktree you will close from.
* **df3a is intermittent, not deterministic**: 259b's close failed twice with an identical empty-object
  payload and succeeded on the third. I was one data point from escalating it wrongly.

--- STATE HANDED OVER ---
* `9790` — Gerrit **1406** (`LLM-Review +1`, Verified pending). All 5 ACs verified against the change.
  Shared stdlib-only `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py`; both consumers DELEGATE, so AC4's drift

comments.body:
## NOTE: the three preceding entries are IDENTICAL DUPLICATES of one session log — read any one

Author error, recorded rather than hidden. I wrapped `session-log append` in a retry loop guarded by
a verification predicate that searched `rebar list` for the log's title. **`rebar list` excludes
`session_log` tickets by design** (its output contains only story/bug/task/epic), so the predicate
could never match, every attempt read as a failure, and the same 10151-byte entry was appended three
times. The store is append-only and there is no comment-delete, so the duplicates stand.

Two lessons, both instances of the same root error I logged four times inside the entry itself:
a verification that CANNOT succeed is indistinguishable from a failure, and I did not check the
predicate against a case known to exist before trusting it to drive a retry loop. `session-log append`
had in fact reported `created: false` each time — i.e. it appended to the existing log successfully.
**I retried against my own broken check instead of reading the command's output**, which is precisely
the failure mode the entry above warns about.

=== HANDOFF: e369 CLOSED (force, documented). What remains is a GATE-DEFECT CLUSTER. ===

--- WHERE THINGS STAND ---
**Epic e369 (Jira Server/DC support) is CLOSED**, 2026-08-05, via `--force-close` on explicit operator
direction, after a manual evidenced verification of all 14 acceptance criteria against `gerrit/main`
(see the "MANUAL AC VERIFICATION" comment on the epic — each criterion checked with a file:line or a
run id, not a checkbox). `signature: None` plus a `FORCE_CLOSE` audit record are present: this close
records **operator authorization + manual verification, NOT a passing completion verification.** Do
not read it as an attestation.

Delivered and verified: **59/59 descendants closed, 0 uncertified** (each carrying a real
`completion-verifier` signature; each change merged through `Verified +1` AND `LLM-Review +1`), and
the exit bar green on `main` — harness run **30986591446** at `0df44dcbc9`: 62 passed, 1 xfailed,
**0 failed, 0 errored**, canary `collected=63 executed=62 skipped=1`.

Closing e369 UNBLOCKED **5796** (DC hardening follow-on) and **708d** (Markdown<->Jira rich text).

--- WHY THE FORCE WAS NECESSARY (do not "just retry" it) ---
The completion verifier **cannot produce a verdict for this epic**. Four exhaustions: 480, 1600,
480-with-the-`search_files`-fix, and an instrumented reproduction. [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] proved
it is NOT capacity:
* Three of four instrumented runs **LOOPED**. SPLIT-A repeated one identical `search_files` call
  **144 times**; SPLIT-B looped 62x on an *honest* `(no matches)`. Repetition wasted 40-70% of every
  pathological run.
* The one clean run (238 distinct / 258 calls, ratio 0.922) exhausts on **genuine breadth** against a
  flat 240-request budget — which, per operator intent (the budget bounds FAILURES, not capacity), is
  correct behaviour rather than a bug to route around.
* A resource exhaustion is **not a verdict**, and the gate's only documented exit from that state is
  `--force-close` — the trap that steers agents into the unattested state the project forbids.

--- THE BLOCKING CHAIN (start here) ---
    c827  wire loop detection to ACT (it is currently report-only)
     |-- 70bc (P1) BLOCKER: `max_consecutive_repeat` is INVERTED — counts only ADJACENT repeats, so a
     |            real 4-call cycle scores 1 while the HEALTHY run scores 5. Wiring an actuator to
     |            today's metric fires on healthy runs and misses real cycles. Replacement proven:
     |            windowed distinct-ratio (field `distinct_ratio_window`, window 24, trip <= 0.50,
     |            order-insensitive) fires on all three pathological runs (calls 88/151/196) and NEVER
     |            on the clean one.
     `-- 895c (P1) BLOCKER: plan-review fails CLOSED on a provider error. Two runs minutes apart, very
                  different plan text, byte-identical failure at `review@then/prerequisite_verify`
                  ("Grammar compilation timed out", Bedrock). One 400 degrades EVERY finding to
                  `no-verification`; no partial credit. CAVEAT: other reviews passed fine the same day
                  (e369, 941b, 8390) — it is NOT globally broken; something about c827's review trips
                  it. Pin that down; do not overclaim.

    aec1 (P1, in progress) usage instrumentation. Mechanism already found (d166, duplicate, linked):
         `usage_log.record()` NO-OPS unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set (unset by default), and `_FIELDS`
         (`usage_log.py:32`) records `requests` but NOT `tool_calls` — the axis separating a loop from
         breadth AND the second kill path. A default-off recorder is functionally no recorder.

--- DESIGN DECISIONS ALREADY TAKEN (do not relitigate) ---
* **Flat forced landing: WITHDRAWN.** It truncates a healthy run and produces a worse verdict on a
  gate that SIGNS. Operator intent: bound failures, not breadth.
* **Finalizer routing: ADOPTED.** Route detection into the shipped tool-free finalizer
  (`completion_recovery.py:453-521`), which assembles clean per-criterion evidence, instead of landing
  on a history that just looped 144 times. Feasibility proven (E5): an exception raised inside the
  toolset filter predicate propagates cleanly and survives in `__cause__`.
  **Caveat that would be a NEW bug:** it currently surfaces as `LLMUnavailableError`, because
  `interpret_failure`'s third branch (`structured_run.py:110-155`) sweeps unrecognised exceptions into
  the provider-outage bucket. A runaway misreported as a provider outage is the exact defect class
  being removed — a typed branch must go AHEAD of that fallback.
* **Both kill paths must be bounded.** `tool_step_limit` gates model REQUESTS; `tool_calls_limit`
  (= 2x request_limit) is a second independent path enforced on PROJECTED usage
  (`pydantic_ai/usage.py:412-419`). Measured: at 3 calls/request, limits of 239, 216 AND 180 all still
  die. A fix setting only `tool_step_limit` passes a 1-call-per-request test and fails in production.
* **The discriminator predicate fires 6x per run step** — memoise once per `run_step`, not per tool.
* **AC-split fallback (two runs, full context, half the ACs each): TESTED, NOT SUFFICIENT alone.**
  Criteria partition cleanly, but both halves still died, and SPLIT-B spent MORE per criterion (23.9)
  than the full run (17.0) — variance swamps the halving. Viable only WITH the actuator. Two
  signatures over disjoint criteria subsets materially changes what an attestation MEANS: that needs
  an operator decision, not a quiet implementation.

--- OPEN DECISIONS FOR THE OPERATOR ---
1. **f020** — keep or delete the dormant absence-probe port. Deleting removes DC's only import of the

2. **AC-split attestation semantics**, if that route is wanted.
3. **How deep to go** on the gate cluster — each defect was found by refusing to force a close, and

--- OTHER OPEN WORK ---
5796 (follow-on epic): 4a6d (a THIRD live-DC channel with the weak readiness gate — it REPORTS rather
than fails, so a fast run silently commits a wrong contract), a3fa (capability casts unguarded), f020.
Unparented by deliberate decision: 6194 / 6a74 / 9a46 (Cloud-surface defects found by DC parity
guards — real, but not DC feature delivery), a9bd (capability-map trust; operator ordered unparented),
8a5e (four MORE vacuous AST guards — third occurrence of the class), ed5e (57 tickets still orphaned
by the 2026-08-03 reconciler parent-clear incident, stuck because their parents are closed).
c827 siblings: fd84, 8b97, 218e, 4c2b, 354d. Plus 6ec8 (child-closure proof computed then hidden from
the verifier), 3787 (P1, Rebase-If-Necessary submits an unvalidated tree), df3a (fix in flight as
Gerrit 1408, another session).

--- OPERATIONAL RULES THAT COST REAL TIME TO LEARN ---
* **CI selects by MARKER**: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`.
  A `tests/unit` path subset MISSES unmarked tests under `tests/integration/` — that gap cost a CI
  cycle (the `EXPECTED_LEAF_PAIRS` drift guard). ~10,400 tests vs ~8,000.
* **`git commit --amend -F -` DROPS the `Change-Id`**, minting a new change instead of a patchset —
  which is how a green-but-WRONG change (1398) was left sitting submittable.
* **3787 discipline**: if `gerrit/main` moved past your base, rebase LOCALLY and re-gate rather than
  letting Gerrit rebase server-side into a tree CI never validated. `main` moved ~every 20-30 min.
* **Store lock contention is real** (ab54/7084): `rebar edit` can fail with `flock: could not acquire
  lock after 60s` and NOT land. Retry, and confirm every write by READING THE OUTPUT.
* **Attestations go `stale-code` once their own change lands** — expect a re-review before every
  close. `--status` is HEAD-relative: run it from the same worktree you will close from.
* **The GitHub mirror LAGS Gerrit.** `gh workflow run --ref main` can resolve to the PRE-merge commit.
  Check the resolved `headSha` against the merge commit before letting a 45-minute run proceed.
* **Agent tools come from the INSTALLED rebar, not the attested snapshot** (`runner.py:341`). After
  merging a fix under `llm/`, confirm the interpreter you will run from actually has it.
* **AN EMPTY OR CLEAN SCAN IS NOT EVIDENCE UNTIL THE SCAN ITSELF IS CHECKED.** Eight false conclusions
  in one session: a regex missing `Jira DC` (space); `rebar list` carrying NO `description` field;
  grepping a stale working tree instead of `gerrit/main`; `grep -oE` splicing across
  `executed=62 skipped=1`; `grep '^FAILED'` defeated by ANSI codes; `grep -c` against a path that did
  not exist; `pgrep` matching its OWN shell wrapper; and a wrong path guess nearly recorded as an AC9
  violation. Control scans in BOTH directions.
* **A mutation check only tests the axes its fixture varies.** Change 1398 passed BOTH gates with a
  real bug because its fixture hardcoded `remote_parent_id: None`.

--- THE FINDINGS THAT OUTLIVE THIS EPIC ---
1. **Gates passing != correct.** 1398 held `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` while containing a bug

2. **`search_files` was LYING repo-wide** (fixed, Gerrit 1433): it returned `(no matches)` whenever

3. **"Computed then discarded" is a pattern, not an incident** — the repetition diagnostic built by

4. **Vacuous guards are a recurring class** — 59b2, then 34c2, and 8a5e documents four more live. A

5. **Authored prose gets read as measurement.** 9790's error message asserted a rule ("no

=== HANDOFF DELTA: aec1 instrumentation implemented (Gerrit 1435, votes pending) ===

**The mechanism is sharper than 'not persisted' — it was COMPUTED AND THROWN AWAY.**
`failure_usage()` (`usage_log.py:136-191`) already reduces a run's messages to the COMPLETE
loop-vs-breadth signal. `record()` then built its row from `_FIELDS` alone (`usage_log.py:32`,
iterated at `:311`), silently dropping SEVEN keys one frame from the write. Proven on a real
exhaustion run through the real runner:

    COMPUTED:  requests=125 tool_calls=125 tool_calls_distinct=1 max_consecutive_repeat=125
               request_limit=125 tool_calls_limit=250 top_repeated=[read_file:9148ca16 x125]
    ON DISK:   op/outcome/model/timestamp + 4 token fields + requests=125   <- nothing else
    DISCARDED: finish_reason, max_consecutive_repeat, request_limit, tool_calls,
               tool_calls_distinct, tool_calls_limit, top_repeated_tool_calls

**A 125/1 loop was recorded indistinguishably from 125 requests of breadth.** That is the fourth
instance of the computed-then-discarded pattern, and the most consequential: it is *why* the budget
could be raised five times blind.

Refinement to the earlier claim: `tool_calls` is not merely missing from `_FIELDS` — it is **passed
into `record()` and discarded**. Not recorded under an alias; the written row's complete key set was
dumped to confirm.

Two further mechanisms: the SUCCESS path never computed shape at all (`_extract_usage` returns 5
keys), and the sink no-ops unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is set — set in only 3 places, none of them an
operator's gate run.

**Fix (Gerrit 1435, votes pending):** a second explicit `_SHAPE_FIELDS` allowlist written
key-only-when-present (absent = 'not measured'; a `0` would falsely assert 'used no tools'); the
success path calls the same reducer via a `run_shape` ALIAS (not a rename — `structured_run.py`'s
call sites belong to the c827 stream); and gate runs record with NO env var via the existing
fail-closed `in_gate_session()` predicate bound at `gate_source.gate_read_root`. Non-gate callers
stay byte-identical.

**Retrieval, proven on a real un-instrumented run:**
`python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl`. With `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` confirmed
unset, `rebar review-plan` wrote 5 rows including
`plan-review-prerequisite-verifier outcome=failed duration_s=185.6 request_limit=125
tool_calls_limit=250` — **a failed call that burned 3 minutes and previously left no trace**, priced
at $0.0412.

**LIMITATION THAT MATTERS FOR [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0]:** these are WHOLE-RUN counts. They
reproduce all four measured ratios, but a **windowed** distinct-ratio needs the signature SEQUENCE,
which is deliberately not stored. Whoever implements 70bc's windowed discriminator must not assume
the record alone suffices.

New sibling: **df94-66ba-dbf8-4ac1** (`discovered_from` aec1) — `failure.py:82-96` admits
`request_limit`/`tool_calls_limit` but neither consumed count; the gate-error sidecar and the
completion-verdict sidecar are both MISSING the counts. Kept separate because `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` is a
sanitization boundary deserving its own privacy review.

State: [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86] is `in_progress`; **Gerrit 1435 must reach `Verified +1` and
`LLM-Review +1` before it closes.** Worktree /Users/joeoakhart/aec1-usage retained (unlanded).
